newsitem.title: UK: Dry cargo starts week slow, mixed.
newsitem.headline: Dry cargo starts week slow, mixed.

text.p: Little change was evident on Monday from last week's trends in the freight market. Caper rates continued to soften and the older smaller geared vessels were not in demand except from S.America where handy rates were edging forward.
Panamax levels were steady worldwide with the Indian Ocean proving potentally the strongest area for owners. The BFI was up 5 points to 1465.

GRAIN - EMC fixed 52,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Japan at the end of last week at $25.75 no combo for March 7/21 but it was widely believed that higher levels have been conceded by other charterers (the BFI panel put the rate at $26.59 combo). Other grain fixtures remained unreported - Glencore with a Caper N. France/Saudi Arabia, for example, and Toepfer with a Panamax Mississippi/Portugal for end Feb loading.

Andre were linked with trade Greece for 45,000 soyabeans Paranagua/Lisbon at $14.50 and with Mister Michael 53,836 dwt delivery prompt Flushing for an E.Coast S.American round at $7,500 daily. Kingston Maritime were said to have taken the relet Stone Topaz 65,029 dwt for 6-8 months in the Atlantic on private terms.

Toepfer were rumoured to have fixed Allalinhorn of 1.5m cft grain Paranagua/Continent at a lumpsum equivalent of $17.50 basis 53' for Feb/March loading and also a vessel of about 1.1m cft at $19.00, but full details were not available. Dreyfus were linked with Megalochari for 28/30,00 heavy grain Baltimore/North Spain for end Feb at a lumpsum equivalent of $12.00, and also with a vessel of 1.3m cft Mississippi/N.France at a lumpsum equivalent of $15.00/15.25.

A fair volume of new business was quoted today - Egyptian charterers for a vessel able to load 50,000 wheat on 38' North France/Egypt for end Feb/early March, NSAC 54,000 heavy grain Pacific North-west to Taiwan Feb 25/March 12 and/or similar ex US Gulf for March 1/15, and Samsun 35/36,000 heavy grain Nopac/Japan for March 1/12. From S.America Glencore quoted enquiry for a Panamax delivery S.Brazil Feb 27/March 3 trip Skaw-Passero and Topefer have 60,000 heavy grain Paranagua/Lisbon-Hamburg range for March 7/14.

MINERALS - Some caper fixtures from the end of last week have remained secret - the Cobelfret vessel Lowlands Rose 170,000 dwt delivery Japan mid March to Bocimar, Curbunesti 171,000 dwt from Taiwan end March, and Georgios M 148,000 dwt from Le Havre early March.

Sidmawere rumoured to have fixed 70,000 coal Hampton Roads/Ghent-Terneuzen but the rate has not emerged. In the Pacific Halla were believed to have booked Yu May 65,000 dwt for 12 months on private terms and the newbuilding Panamax Nol Sheda was also understood fixed on timecharter for short period.
Full Comfort 70,180 dwt was taken by Iino delivery Richards Bay early March for a coal trip to Japan at a firm $12,500 daily plus $300,000 bonus.

HANDY-SIZES - Generally the smaller old types under 30,000 dwt remain stuck in a weak market worldwide except for Brazil and Argentina. Some period business was reported today - R.A. Oetker were said to have booked an over-age 38,000 dwt vessel delivery Hamburg end Feb for 2 or 3 laden legs Atlantic trading at $5,500 daily, and the 1977-built Maria Topic 37,226 dwt was linked with Van Ommeren for 9-11 months at $7,500 daily, although delivery details were lacking.

In the east Navix Asia fixed Olympic Miracle 29,000 dwt delivery NoPac early March trip Japan at $7,250 daily plus $142,500 bonus, and a sister vessel Olympic Mentor open prompt Bangkok was fixed on subjects for an Australian round.
